title: Telegram markdown renderer — convergence report
markdown:
# Telegram markdown renderer — convergence report

Echo ran 6 review iterations (4 internal rounds + external cross-model with GPT/Gemini/Grok + 2 final consistency passes). The spec is converged and ready for your approval.

## What it does, in plain terms

Dawn fixed Telegram message rendering on her side with a client-side script. This spec brings the same fix to instar, but on the server so every send path benefits — jobs, dispatches, alerts, lifeline pings, and shell scripts all go through the same formatter. Bold becomes bold, tables render with aligned monospace, links become real links, headings become bold text, bullets get a • character.

It also does one bigger thing: switches instar's Telegram parse mode from legacy Markdown to HTML. To make rollback safe, a `legacy-passthrough` mode preserves every callsite's original parse mode byte-for-byte — one config flip reverts to exactly today's behavior.

## What the reviewers caught

- **Critical**: my original premise was wrong. I assumed instar sent as HTML; it actually sends mostly as legacy Markdown with ONE callsite already on HTML. Integration reviewer caught this and the whole spec was rewritten.
- **Critical**: "one sendMessage funnel" was also wrong. There are two separate `apiCall()` methods (adapter + lifeline, different Bot API clients). Spec now wires both.
- **Critical**: my original pipeline ran formatting before the rewrite gates. GPT/adversarial caught that the LLM-based gates can corrupt HTML bytes. Reordered to format LAST.
- **High**: Wikipedia-style URLs with parens would break the link regex. Gemini caught it. Replaced with balanced-paren scanner.
- **High**: plain-retry on Bot API 400 would double-escape or collide idempotency keys. Fixed: retry from raw text with a `fallback-plain` key suffix.
- **High**: `editMessageText` cannot be split into multiple messages. Added explicit error path.
- Plus ~30 other findings across security, scalability, adversarial, integration.

## What happens next

If you approve, I open PR1 (formatter module + tests + legacy-passthrough mode shipped disabled) followed by PR2 (wire into both chokepoints + shell template + canary flip on Echo's agent first, with eyeball verification at 1h/6h/24h before the default flips for all agents).

Rollback is a one-line config flip to `legacy-passthrough`. No code revert, no redeploy, preserves pre-change behavior exactly.

## Approval

The spec is tagged converged. To approve, flip `approved: true` in its frontmatter (or tell me to do it after you've read it). Until approved, `/instar-dev` is blocked from touching source code on this spec — that's the structural gate working correctly.
